I'll add two new test cases for edge cases in the date math functionality. These will cover leap year boundaries and month/year transitions.

First, I'll add a test for a date that crosses into a leap year boundary:

```python
def test_add_days_leap_year_boundary():
    """Test adding days that crosses into a leap year boundary."""
    # Test going from end of a non-leap year to start of a leap year
    date = datetime(2023, 12, 31)
    result = add_days(date, 1)
    assert result == datetime(2024, 1, 1)
    
    # Test going from end of a leap year to start of next year
    date = datetime(2024, 12, 31)
    result = add_days(date, 1)
    assert result == datetime(2025, 1, 1)
```

Next, I'll add a test for the number of days in February during a leap year:

```python
def test_days_in_month_leap_year():
    """Test getting days in February during a leap year."""
    assert days_in_month(2024, 2) == 29
    assert is_leap_year(2024) is True
    
    # Test a non-leap year for comparison
    assert days_in_month(2023, 2) == 28
    assert is_leap_year(2023) is False
```

These edge cases cover:
1. Date transitions between years (especially leap year boundaries)
2. Correct handling of February in leap years (29 days vs 28 days)

The tests will verify that the date math functions correctly handle these boundary conditions that are not covered in the existing basic tests.
